command.summary: Creates a new Azure Cosmos DB database account.

parameters.name: --name
parameters.help: Name of the Cosmos DB database account.

parameters.name: --resource-group
parameters.help: Name of resource group. You can configure the default group using `az configure --defaults group=<name>`.

parameters.name: --assign-identity
parameters.help: Assign system or user assigned identities separated by spaces. Use '[system]' to refer system assigned identity.

parameters.name: --capabilities
parameters.help: Set custom capabilities on the Cosmos DB database account.

parameters.name: --default-consistency-level
parameters.help: Default consistency level of the Cosmos DB database account.

parameters.name: --default-identity
parameters.help: The primary identity to access key vault in CMK related features. e.g. 'FirstPartyIdentity', 'SystemAssignedIdentity' and more. User-assigned identities are specified in format `UserAssignedIdentity=<resource ID of the user- assigned identity>`.

parameters.name: --default-priority-level
parameters.help: Default Priority Level of Request if not specified.

parameters.name: --disable-key-based-metadata-write-access
parameters.help: Disable write operations on metadata resources (databases, containers, throughput) via account keys.

parameters.name: --disable-local-auth
parameters.help: Disable key-based authentication on the Cosmos DB account.

parameters.name: --enable-analytical-storage
parameters.help: Flag to enable log storage on the account.

parameters.name: --enable-automatic-failover
parameters.help: Enables automatic failover of the write region in the rare event that the region is unavailable due to an outage. Automatic failover will result in a new write region for the account and is chosen based on the failover priorities configured for the account.

parameters.name: --enable-burst-capacity
parameters.help: Flag to Enable/Disable burst capacity feature. Usage: --enable-burst-capacity true
parameters.default: false The accepted values for the enable-burst-capacity are true and false

parameters.name: --enable-free-tier
parameters.help: If enabled the account is free-tier. WARNING: Argument '--enable-free-tier' is in preview and under development. Reference and support levels: https://aka.ms/CLI_refstatus

parameters.name: --enable-multiple-write-locations
parameters.help: Enable Multiple Write Locations.

parameters.name: --enable-partition-merge
parameters.help: Flag to enable partition merge on the account.

parameters.name: --enable-pbe
parameters.help: Flag to enable priority based execution on the account.

parameters.name: --enable-prpp-autoscale
parameters.help: Flag to Enable/Disable burst capacity feature. Usage: --enable-prpp-autoscale true
parameters.default: false The accepted values for the --enable-prpp-autoscale are true and false

parameters.name: --enable-virtual-network
parameters.help: Enables virtual network on the Cosmos DB database account.

parameters.name: --ip-range-filter
parameters.help: Firewall support. Specifies the set of IP addresses or IP address ranges in CIDR form to be included as the allowed list of client IPs for a given database account. IP addresses/ranges must be comma-separated and must not contain any spaces.

parameters.name: --key-uri
parameters.help: The URI of the key vault.

parameters.name: --kind
parameters.help: The type of Cosmos DB database account to create.

parameters.name: --locations
parameters.help: Add a location to the Cosmos DB database account. Usage: --locations KEY=VALUE [KEY=VALUE...] Required Keys: regionName, failoverPriority Optional Key: isZoneRedundant Failover priority values are 0 for write regions and greater than 0 for read regions. A failover priority value must be unique and less than the total number of regions. Multiple locations can be specified by using more than one `--locations` argument.
parameters.default: single region account in the location of the specified resource group

parameters.name: --max-interval
parameters.help: When used with Bounded Staleness consistency, this value represents the time amount of staleness (in seconds) tolerated. Accepted range for this value is 5 - 86400.

parameters.name: --max-staleness-prefix
parameters.help: When used with Bounded Staleness consistency, this value represents the number of stale requests tolerated. Accepted range for this value is 10 - 2,147,483,647.

parameters.name: --minimal-tls-version
parameters.help: Indicate the minimum allowed TLS version. Usage: --minimal-tls-version TLSVersion
parameters.default: Tls, except for Cassandra and Mongo APIs, which only work with Tls12 The accepted values for the minimal TLS version are 'Tls', 'Tls11', and 'Tls12', which correspond to the TLS versions 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2

parameters.name: --network-acl-bypass
parameters.help: Flag to enable or disable Network Acl Bypass.

parameters.name: --network-acl-bypass-resource-ids
parameters.help: List of Resource Ids to allow Network Acl Bypass.

parameters.name: --public-network-access
parameters.help: Sets public network access in server to either Enabled, Disabled, or SecuredByPerimeter.

parameters.name: --server-version
parameters.help: Valid only for MongoDB accounts.

parameters.name: --tags
parameters.help: Space-separated tags: key[=value] [key[=value]...]. Use '' to clear existing tags.

parameters.name: --virtual-network-rules
parameters.help: ACL's for virtual network.

parameters.name: --analytical-storage-schema-type
parameters.help: Schema type for analytical storage.

parameters.name: --backup-interval
parameters.help: The frequency(in minutes) with which backups are taken (only for accounts with periodic mode backups).

parameters.name: --backup-policy-type
parameters.help: The type of backup policy of the account to create.

parameters.name: --backup-redundancy
parameters.help: The redundancy type of the backup Storage account.

parameters.name: --backup-retention
parameters.help: The time(in hours) for which each backup is retained (only for accounts with periodic mode backups).

parameters.name: --continuous-tier
parameters.help: The tier of Continuous backup.

parameters.name: --acquire-policy-token
parameters.help: Acquiring an Azure Policy token automatically for this resource operation.

parameters.name: --change-reference
parameters.help: The related change reference ID for this resource operation.

parameters.name: --databases-to-restore
parameters.help: Add a database and its collection names to restore. Usage: --databases-to-restore name=DatabaseName collections=collection1 [collection2...].

parameters.name: --gremlin-databases-to-restore
parameters.help: Add a gremlin database and its graph names to restore. Usage: --gremlin-databases-to-restore name=DatabaseName graphs=graph1 [graph2...].

parameters.name: --is-restore-request
parameters.help: Restore from an existing/deleted account.

parameters.name: --restore-source
parameters.help: The restorable-database-account Id of the source account from which the account has to be restored. Required if --is-restore-request is set to true.

parameters.name: --restore-timestamp
parameters.help: The timestamp to which the account has to be restored to. Required if --is-restore-request is set to true.

parameters.name: --tables-to-restore
parameters.help: Add table names to restore. Usage: --tables-to-restore tables=table1 [table2...].

parameters.name: --debug
parameters.help: Increase logging verbosity to show all debug logs.

parameters.name: --help
parameters.help: Show this help message and exit.

parameters.name: --only-show-errors
parameters.help: Only show errors, suppressing warnings.

parameters.name: --output
parameters.help: Output format.

parameters.name: --query
parameters.help: JMESPath query string. See http://jmespath.org/ for more information and examples.

parameters.name: --subscription
parameters.help: Name or ID of subscription. You can configure the default subscription using `az account set -s NAME_OR_ID`.

parameters.name: --verbose
parameters.help: Increase logging verbosity. Use --debug for full debug logs.
